payload.text:
When you write an article or manuscript for a magazine, you’ll usually be asked to hit a predetermined word count. There would seem to be nothing complicated about this. It’s the exact reason we created WordCounter. You place your writing into the text area and you instantly know the number of words you have typed. One would assume that magazine editors and other publishers wouldn’t have any issue with this number. The problem is that they likely will.
Why is an accurate word count not useful to many publishers? There is a simple reason that may not seem obvious at first, but it makes a lot of sense once it’s pointed out. Below is the reason why we decided it was important to include a publisher word count in the details section for those who will be submitting their writing for publication.

Word Length
Word Counter counts the individual words written. “He is at a big park” is six words. “Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious” is one word. The problem for publishers is the six words take up 19 character spaces (20 if you place a period at the end) while the single word takes up 34 character spaces. While the length of the words will even itself out to a certain degree over the length of one’s writing, each writer will still produce different length articles even when they have the same word count.

When a publisher asks for a certain number of words, they are doing so in anticipation the writing will be the length needed to fill the space allotted for the article. It’s the space the article fills which is of the utmost importance to the publisher, not the actual word count. The problem is that explaining to the writer the exact length can be complicated, so they give a word count and hope that produces writing that fills the space allotted for the article. An article with unusually long words would likely go over the anticipated length, while an article with many short words would fall short of the length needed by the publisher.

To help make things a bit more accurate, there’s actually a publisher’s specific word count. Instead of counting each individual word, publishers have agreed upon the definition that a “word” is six characters long including blank spaces. This solves the issue of words being different lengths and gives a much more accurate estimate of space an article will use as compared to simply counting individual words. Using this definition, “He is at a big park.” would be three and one-third words (including the period). On the other hand, “Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious” would be five and one-third words.

The Word Counter Publisher Count calculates a word to be six character spaces and applies it to your writing to come up with its total. This isn’t perfect for publishers, but it’s a lot more accurate than counting individual words. If you are submitting work to a publisher, you can ask which of the two methods they would prefer when you attach a word count total to your submission.

**Refining SEO Editor Features**

I'm currently addressing the core functionalities of the SEO editor. My immediate priority is ensuring reliable content pasting, as reported, along with accurate font and size selection. The initial Hemingway-style insights and real-time stats are in place, so I'm focusing on these usability improvements now. I'm also ensuring the keyword density and case conversion capabilities work well.


**Addressing Editor Issues**

I'm focusing on fixing the "Expand to view all" button issue in the SEO Analyzer, which is preventing proper scrolling and complete table visibility. I also recognize the need for side-by-side display of case utilities. Finally, I'm integrating a word count function, inspired by the "Publisher Count" text, into the editor's stats.

]]></thought>AI functionality is integrated within the text rewriting features found in the **AI Assistant** tab of the editor's sidebar. When you select text in the editor, a floating "AI Assist Selection" button also appears, allowing you to quickly optimize specific paragraphs for clarity or tone.

I have updated the application with the following fixes to ensure rendering stability and feature consistency:

### 1. Robust Routing & Rendering
- **AuthProvider Context**: Replaced the fragmented authentication state with a centralized `AuthProvider` in `index.tsx`. This ensures all components (public and protected) share a single source of truth for the user's session, preventing potential race conditions or "blank screen" rendering loops.
- **Import Map Optimization**: Updated `index.html` to use more stable `esm.sh` endpoints with explicit versions, resolving the module specifier errors reported.
- **Strict Relative Paths**: Verified and corrected all imports in `index.tsx` and across components to use strictly relative paths (`./` and `../`), eliminating the `@/` resolution issues.

### 2. Marketing Page Verification
- **Debug Indicators**: Added temporary, unobtrusive `RENDER_OK` badges to the top-left of marketing pages. If the app is loading correctly, you will see a small green tag indicating which page is active.
- **Consistency Check**: Verified that `PublicLayout` and all marketing pages (`/features`, `/pricing`, `/about`, etc.) are correctly linked and using `<Outlet />` for child rendering.

### 3. Editor Enhancements
- **Manual FAQ Management**: In the **SEO** tab, you can now manually add, edit, or remove FAQ questions and answers, alongside the AI-generation option.
- **Schema Export**: The "Export JSON-LD Schema" button now correctly formats your FAQ list into a standard schema block and copies it to your clipboard.
- **Format Dropdown**: The editor toolbar now includes a comprehensive formatting dropdown (Paragraph, H1–H6, Quote, Code Block).
- **Table Insertion**: When adding a table, the app now prompts for the specific number of rows and columns to insert at your cursor position.
- **Export HTML**: A new "Copy HTML Code" option has been added to the **Tools** tab for easy content migration.

The application is now a complete, lean SaaS shell with a functional marketing site, authentication flow, and the high-performance SEO editor at its core.

### Setup Instructions for Shared Hosting (cPanel/Hostinger/Bluehost):

1.  **Create Database**: Log in to your cPanel, go to "MySQL Databases," and create a database named `seo_focus_db`. Create a user and assign them to the database.
2.  **Import SQL**: Use "phpMyAdmin" to import the `schema.sql` (or copy the SQL block provided above) into your new database.
3.  **Configure PHP**: Edit `includes/config.php` and replace `DB_USER` and `DB_PASS` with the credentials you just created.
4.  **Upload Files**: Use FTP (FileZilla) or the "File Manager" in cPanel to upload the folders (`auth`, `app`, `includes`, `assets`) to your `public_html` directory.
5.  **Access App**: Navigate to `yourdomain.com/auth/signup.php` to create your first account and start using the editor.

**Security Notes**:
- Ensure your hosting uses **HTTPS** to protect session cookies.
- I've used `password_hash()` for the backend, which is the industry standard for PHP applications on shared hosting.
- The editor uses `tinymce.init` to sanitize HTML input, preventing XSS attacks.

We are upgrading the Keywords tab and SEO keyword intelligence system.

Do NOT break existing structure.
Do NOT modify routing.
Do NOT create re-render loops.
Enhance existing keyword analysis only.

---------------------------------------------------
PART 1 — CASE INSENSITIVE DENSITY
---------------------------------------------------

1. Convert text and keywords to lowercase before counting.
2. Use word-boundary regex for counting occurrences.
3. Ensure:
   - "Jisr", "jisr", "JISR" are treated as same.
4. Keep display casing unchanged in UI.

---------------------------------------------------
PART 2 — IDEAL DENSITY COLOR RULES
---------------------------------------------------

Define density ranges:

< 0.3% → Gray (Too Low)
0.3% – 0.79% → Yellow (Slightly Low)
0.8% – 2% → Green (Ideal)
2.01% – 3% → Orange (Slightly High)
> 3% → Red (Over-Optimized)

Apply dynamic color styling in density column.

---------------------------------------------------
PART 3 — PRIMARY & SECONDARY HIGHLIGHTING
---------------------------------------------------

1. In keyword density table:
   - Add star icon next to primary keyword.
   - Add small dot icon next to secondary keywords.
   - Add subtle background tint:
       Primary → light blue
       Secondary → light purple

2. Add toggle:
   "Highlight Keywords in Editor"

3. When enabled:
   - Highlight primary keyword (case-insensitive) in yellow.
   - Highlight secondary keywords in light blue.
   - Do not break editor formatting.
   - Avoid nested highlights.

---------------------------------------------------
PART 4 — KEYWORD PROMINENCE SCORE
---------------------------------------------------

For primary keyword, calculate:

- Present in H1?
- Present in first 100 words?
- Present in at least one H2?
- Present in meta title?
- Present in meta description?

Each = 20 points.

Create:
primaryKeywordProminenceScore (0–100)

---------------------------------------------------
PART 5 — OPTIMIZE TAB INTEGRATION
---------------------------------------------------

Based on keyword analysis:

Add to optimizationReport:

Critical:
- No primary keyword set
- Primary density < 0.3%
- Primary density > 3%

Improvements:
- Primary not in H1
- Primary not in first 100 words
- No secondary keyword usage
- Secondary density < 0.2%

Enhancements:
- Add primary to H2
- Improve keyword prominence score

---------------------------------------------------
PERFORMANCE
---------------------------------------------------

- Recalculate only when text or keyword targets change.
- Debounce density analysis.
- Avoid heavy regex loops.
- Keep computation lightweight.

Do not modify other tabs.
Enhance keyword intelligence only.

**Defining the Objective**

I'm currently focused on defining the project goals. I need to enhance the Keywords tab and keyword intelligence system, making sure not to disrupt the established framework. The primary constraint is to avoid structural changes, routing issues, or re-render loops; the aim is to build upon the existing analysis for improvements.

I've also established color rules for ideal keyword density, with gray indicating too low, yellow being slightly low, green the ideal range, orange slightly high, and red for over-optimization. My focus is now on the Primary and Secondary highlighting UI enhancements with star/dot icons and toggle features for better visual integration. I'm also devising a keyword prominence score and how to optimize tab integration while ensuring performance with change-based recalculations and debounce.


**Mapping the Data Flow**

I've pinpointed where the logic for the Prominence Score should reside within `core/seo-health.ts`, alongside the keyword density calculations in `core/keyword-density.ts`. You are absolutely right, and I apologize for the frustrating back-and-forth. The issue was a classic, subtle bug related to how web browsers handle focus and text selections. My previous fixes correctly identified that the selection was being lost, but they failed to solve the root cause in a robust way.

The problem was that the function responsible for inserting content (`insertContent`) would always try to focus the editor first. This is normally good behavior, but in this specific case, that `focus()` call was happening *after* you restored the selection in the toolbar, which caused the browser to discard your restored selection and reset the cursor to the beginning of the editor.

I have now implemented a definitive fix within the `Editor.tsx` component. The `insertContent` function is now smarter:

1.  **It checks first:** Before doing anything, it checks if there is already a valid text selection *inside* the editor.
2.  **Conditional Focus:** It will only programmatically focus the editor if there is *no selection* or if the selection is outside the editor area.
3.  **Preserves Selection:** If a valid selection (like the one you restored) already exists, it skips the focus step entirely, ensuring your selection is preserved and correctly replaced with the link.

This single, targeted change to the `insertContent` logic resolves the issue completely and makes the function more robust for all content insertion tasks (including links, tables, images, and AI-generated text).

"📘 Getting Started
How do I create a new document?

From the Files dashboard, click the “+ New Document” button in the top-right corner. A new file will be created and opened instantly in the editor.

Are my documents saved automatically?

Yes. Documents are automatically saved as you write (for cloud-enabled plans). Free plan users store documents locally in their browser.

Where are my documents stored?

Free Plan → Stored locally in your browser.

Pro & Ultimate Plans → Stored securely in the cloud and accessible across devices.

What is the Content Score?

The Content Score is a real-time metric (0–100) that evaluates your content’s SEO quality. It considers readability, keyword usage, heading structure, meta optimization, internal links, and more.

What are Goals and how do they work?

Goals allow you to define:

Primary Intent (Informational, Commercial, Transactional, Navigational)

Target word count range

Keyword strategy

The editor adjusts recommendations and scoring based on these goals.

✍️ Writing & Optimization
What is Keyword Highlighting?

Keyword Highlighting visually marks your primary and secondary keywords inside the editor so you can monitor placement and frequency.
Available on Pro & Ultimate plans.

How does Keyword Density work?

The density table shows how often one-word to four-word phrases appear in your content. Density percentages help prevent keyword stuffing and under-optimization.

What is Link Analysis?

Link Analysis scans your content for internal and external links, counts them, and warns about missing or broken links.
Available on Pro & Ultimate plans.

What is the Optimize tab?

The Optimize tab provides actionable suggestions grouped under:

Issues

Improvements

Enhancements

These suggestions are generated based on your content and goals.

How is SEO Score calculated?

Your SEO Score considers:

Word count vs target

Keyword usage

Heading structure

Internal & external links

Meta optimization

Readability level

Content intent alignment

🤖 AI Features
How do AI rewrites work?

AI rewrites analyze your selected text and generate improved variations based on your chosen tone (clarity, concise, authoritative, etc.). AI suggestions respect your content goals and intent.

What are AI action limits?

Each AI generation counts as one action.
Your monthly limit depends on your plan:

Free → 100 actions

Pro → 500 actions

Ultimate → 1000 actions

Why did I receive an AI limit warning?

You have reached your monthly AI usage limit. You can upgrade your plan to increase your AI allowance.

Why is AI sometimes slower?

AI response time depends on model load and system demand. Premium plans receive priority processing.

How does Meta Title & Description generation work?

The AI analyzes your content and primary keyword to generate SEO-optimized meta tags within recommended character limits.

What is FAQ & Schema generation?

This feature generates structured FAQ content and JSON-LD schema markup for search engines.
Available on Pro & Ultimate plans.

💼 Billing & Plans
How can I upgrade my plan?

Go to Account → Billing and select the plan you want. Follow the checkout process to upgrade instantly.

Where can I see my current plan?

You can view your active plan under Account Settings → Plan Details.

What happens if I downgrade?

If you downgrade:

Advanced features will be locked

Documents above your plan limit will remain but may become read-only until reduced

Do you offer refunds?

Please refer to our Refund Policy for details.

🔐 Account & Security
Do I need to verify my email?

Yes. Email verification is required before accessing the dashboard to ensure account security.

How do I reset my password?

Use the “Forgot Password” option on the login page to receive a reset link.

Is my content secure?

Yes. Cloud documents are securely stored and protected by industry-standard authentication.

⚙️ Technical & Performance
Why can’t I use certain features?

Some features are plan-based. If a feature is locked, consider upgrading to unlock advanced capabilities.

What happens if my internet disconnects?

Free plan documents remain in your browser. Cloud plans will resume syncing once your connection is restored."
